front.title: Agent Service Function Chain (A-SFC): Architecture and Problem Statement

abstract.t:
Large Language Model (LLM) agents granted write access to tools are emerging as a new class of network participants. Their integrated nature of autonomous decision-making and execution introduces challenges such as compliance bypass and uncontrolled risks. Existing safeguards are mostly application-layer configurable policies residing in the same trust plane as the agent, and are vulnerable to software defects, unintended invocation paths, and bypass via direct connections. Meanwhile, dynamic branching and cross-domain task interactions are pervasive in multi-agent collaboration scenarios. Traditional networks only support flow- level quality awareness and cannot provide task-level end-to-end traceability, fault localization, and quality assurance.
This document defines the A-SFC (Agent Service Function Chain) architecture, which elevates compliance from a "configurable policy" to a "topological fact". Through SRv6 segment routing, mandatory ordered compliance steps are compiled into network forwarding paths; packets that skip compliance gates are dropped directly at the forwarding plane, without relying on cooperation from the agent side. On this basis, this document further introduces a task-level in-situ flow telemetry mechanism. Through three-tier task encoding, it achieves layered quality awareness and fault localization at the link level, agent level, and task level, supporting end-to-end auditability and traceability of multi-agent delegation chains. This document describes the core problems addressed by A-SFC, its overall architecture, key technical components, operating mechanisms, and typical application scenarios.
